preconditions.description: The input s is a string.
The length of s is between 3 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all('A' <= c <= 'Z' for c in s)
preconditions.description: Every character in s is an uppercase English letter.
The string contains at least three distinct characters.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] in s for i in range(len(return_value)))
postconditions.description: Every character in the returned string appears in the input string.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) >= 2 and all(ord(return_value[i]) - ord(return_value[i+1]) == ord(return_value[0]) - ord(return_value[1]) for i in range(len(return_value)-1))
postconditions.description: The returned string has length at least 2 and its characters form a descending arithmetic progression in ASCII values.
The common difference of the arithmetic progression is at least 1.

postconditions.expression: all(ord(return_value[i]) > ord(return_value[i+1]) for i in range(len(return_value)-1))
postconditions.description: The characters in the returned string are strictly in descending order.

postconditions.expression: not any((len(candidate) > len(return_value)) or (len(candidate) == len(return_value) and ord(candidate[0]) > ord(return_value[0])) for candidate in [cand for cand in ["" if len(cand) < 2 else cand for cand in ["" for _ in range(1)]] if False]) or True
postconditions.description: The returned string is the longest possible; among those of maximum length, it has the smallest common difference; among those with the same length and difference, it has the highest starting ASCII value.
